description: Find hotels, flights and flight-and-hotel packages on Vuelo for a destination, dates and number of travellers, within a budget. The results appear in the Vuelo card, where the traveller compares and books them: do not follow up with a question asking which one they want. Hotels are live; pass origin and destinationAirport (IATA codes) to include flights and packages. Flight fares are live and ticketed at purchase. Pass cabin for premium economy, business or first. Returns prices, photos and the payment options Vuelo offers for each trip. Show payment options exactly as returned and always show the full price. Call it ONCE for what the traveller asked: every call shows another Vuelo card in the chat. Do not run extra searches for other towns, dates or budgets on your own; if the request is broad ("somewhere near London"), pick the best single destination or ask the traveller, and search again only when they ask for something different.

airline.description: Flights: an airline the traveller names ("Virgin", "BA"): its flights are listed first. A name or its two-letter code.

cabin.description: Which cabin to price flights in, when the traveller asks for one ("business class", "premium economy", "first"). Economy when not said. Only affects flights and packages.

destination.description: Town or city, with its country when the name is shared or could be ambiguous: "Lisbon", "Zurich, Switzerland", "Cambridge, UK". A region (the Cotswolds) cannot be searched: use one town in it.

destinationAirport.description: Arrival airport for the destination, for example LIS for Lisbon; for a city with several airports (London, Paris, New York, Milan, Rome, Tokyo, Stockholm) pass the city to search them all.

directOnly.description: Flights: only nonstop flights, when the traveller asks for direct or nonstop.

hotel.description: The hotel, when the traveller names one ("the Pulitzer", "The Savoy"): its name only, with the town in destination. Vuelo finds it by name and lists it first, with other hotels in the town after it. Never use minStars or a budget to stand in for a named hotel.

minStars.description: Minimum hotel star rating, when the traveller asks for one (for example 5 for "5-star").

mobile.description: The traveller's mobile number (any country; international format such as +1 415 555 2671 outside the UK), whenever you already know it from this conversation or about the user. Always pass it if you have it: when they tap Book in the Vuelo card, Vuelo texts the secure link straight to it, so they type nothing. Vuelo keeps it for this conversation only and never shows it in the chat. Do not ask for it just to search.

only.description: What the traveller asked for. Set "flights" whenever they ask for flights and not a hotel (for example "find me flights to Nice"), "stays" for a hotel only, "packages" for flight and hotel together. Only leave it out when they want to see everything. Never add hotels to a flights request.

origin.description: Where they fly from, to include live flights and packages: an airport code (LHR) or, when the traveller names a city, the city (London, or LON), which searches every airport there (Heathrow, Gatwick, Stansted, Luton, City). Pass the city unless they named one airport. Ask where they are flying from if they want flights.

passengers.description: Pass this whenever you know it: the results page and checkout then need nothing typed. Who is flying, if the traveller has already told you or you know it: full names as on the passport, and dates of birth if you have them. Vuelo fills these into the booking form so they are not asked for again. Names alone still help. This is who is flying; travellers above is how many.

refundableOnly.description: Only stays with a refundable rate, when the traveller asks for refundable or free cancellation. Flights are ticketed at booking, so none are refundable.

to.description: Check-out or return date, YYYY-MM-DD. For a one-way flight, give the same date as from.

traveller.description: The person booking, whenever you know them from this conversation or about the user: full name as on their ID, email, date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD) and home postcode. Vuelo keeps them for this conversation, so when the traveller taps Book in the card they have nothing to type. Never guess any of it.
